# A marker or requirement that ends with a line break is accepted without complaint

## What happens now
When I give the library a marker or a package requirement that ends with a line break, it accepts the text and gives me a result. It does not tell me that the text is not valid. I ran the current code with a marker and a requirement that each ended with a line break, and both were accepted with no error.

## What should happen
When the text ends with a line break, I should get the normal error that says the input is not valid. When the text ends with ordinary spaces or tabs, it should still be accepted and treated as if those spaces and tabs were not there.

## About this project
This project is a Python library for working with Python package metadata. It reads and checks things like version numbers, package requirements, and environment markers. Many other tools use it to decide which packages to install and how to compare their versions.

## Problem this solves
When a stray line break sneaks into a requirement or a marker, for example one copied out of a file, the library accepts it silently. That hides the mistake and makes it hard to find where the bad text came from.

## What changed
A marker or a requirement that ends with a line break is now reported as an error instead of being accepted. Trailing spaces and tabs are still accepted and ignored, just as they are today.

## Impact
Correctness and ease of use.

## User experience
Before, I pass a requirement that ends with a line break and it is accepted, so I never notice the stray break. After, the same text gives me an error, so I can spot and fix the extra line break right away.

## Hints
- /workspace/src/packaging/_tokenizer.py
- /workspace/tests/test_markers.py
- /workspace/tests/test_requirements.py

 161 │ def _normalize_extras(
 162 │     result: MarkerList | MarkerAtom | str,
 163 │ ) -> MarkerList | MarkerAtom | str:
 164 │     if isinstance(result, list):
 165 │         return [_normalize_extras(r) for r in result]

 167 │         return result

 169 │     lhs, op, rhs = result
 170 │     if isinstance(lhs, Variable) and lhs.value == "extra" and isinstance(rhs, Value):
 171 │         normalized_extra = canonicalize_name(rhs.value)
 172 │         rhs = Value(normalized_extra)
 173 │     elif isinstance(rhs, Variable) and rhs.value == "extra" and isinstance(lhs, Value):
 174 │         normalized_extra = canonicalize_name(lhs.value)
 175 │         lhs = Value(normalized_extra)

 177 │         isinstance(rhs, Variable)
 178 │         and rhs.value in MARKERS_ALLOWING_SET
 179 │         and isinstance(lhs, Value)

 181 │         # PEP 685 (extras) / PEP 735 (dependency_groups): the set-valued membership
 182 │         # literal must also be normalized. evaluate() already canonicalizes both
 183 │         # operands for these keys (see _normalize), so normalizing the literal at

 185 │         # Marker('"Foo" in extras') and Marker('"foo" in extras') must compare and
 186 │         # hash equal (the membership variable is always the right-hand operand).
 187 │         lhs = Value(canonicalize_name(lhs.value))

 191 │ def _normalize_extra_values(results: MarkerList) -> MarkerList:

 193 │     Normalize extra values.

 196 │     return [_normalize_extras(r) for r in results]

 199 │ def _format_marker(
 200 │     marker: list[str] | MarkerAtom | str, first: bool | None = True
 201 │ ) -> str:
 202 │     assert isinstance(marker, (list, tuple, str))
 203 │ 
 204 │     # Unwrap a redundant [[...]] wrapper, but keep the nesting context so a
 205 │     # nested group keeps the parentheses its and/or precedence needs.
 206 │     if (
 207 │         isinstance(marker, list)
 208 │         and len(marker) == 1
 209 │         and isinstance(marker[0], (list, tuple))
 210 │     ):
 211 │         return _format_marker(marker[0], first=first)
 212 │ 
 213 │     if isinstance(marker, list):
 214 │         inner = (_format_marker(m, first=False) for m in marker)
 215 │         if first:
 216 │             return " ".join(inner)
 217 │         else:
 218 │             return "(" + " ".join(inner) + ")"
 219 │     elif isinstance(marker, tuple):
 220 │         return " ".join([m.serialize() for m in marker])
 221 │     else:
 222 │         return marker
 223 │ 
 224 │ 
 225 │ _operators: dict[str, Operator] = {
 226 │     "in": lambda lhs, rhs: lhs in rhs,
 227 │     "not in": lambda lhs, rhs: lhs not in rhs,
 228 │     "<": lambda _lhs, _rhs: False,
 229 │     "<=": operator.eq,
 230 │     "==": operator.eq,
 231 │     "!=": operator.ne,
 232 │     ">=": operator.eq,
 233 │     ">": lambda _lhs, _rhs: False,
 234 │ }

 237 │ def _eval_op(lhs: str, op: Op, rhs: str | AbstractSet[str], *, key: str) -> bool:
 238 │     op_str = op.serialize()
 239 │     if key in MARKERS_REQUIRING_VERSION:
 240 │         try:
 241 │             spec = Specifier(f"{op_str}{rhs}")
 242 │         except InvalidSpecifier:
 243 │             pass
 244 │         else:
 245 │             return spec.contains(lhs, prereleases=True)
 246 │ 
 247 │     oper: Operator | None = _operators.get(op_str)
 248 │     if oper is None:
 249 │         raise UndefinedComparison(f"Undefined {op!r} on {lhs!r} and {rhs!r}.")
 250 │ 
 251 │     return oper(lhs, rhs)

 254 │ def _normalize(
 255 │     lhs: str, rhs: str | AbstractSet[str], key: str
 256 │ ) -> tuple[str, str | AbstractSet[str]]:
 257 │     # PEP 685 - Comparison of extra names for optional distribution dependencies
 258 │     # https://peps.python.org/pep-0685/
 259 │     # > When comparing extra names, tools MUST normalize the names being
 260 │     # > compared using the semantics outlined in PEP 503 for names
 261 │     if key == "extra":
 262 │         assert isinstance(rhs, str), "extra value must be a string"
 263 │         # Both sides are normalized at this point already
 264 │         return (lhs, rhs)
 265 │     if key in MARKERS_ALLOWING_SET:
 266 │         if isinstance(rhs, str):  # pragma: no cover
 267 │             return (canonicalize_name(lhs), canonicalize_name(rhs))
 268 │         else:
 269 │             return (canonicalize_name(lhs), {canonicalize_name(v) for v in rhs})
 270 │ 
 271 │     # other environment markers don't have such standards
 272 │     return lhs, rhs

 274 │ 
 275 │ def _lookup_environment(
 276 │     environment: dict[str, str | AbstractSet[str]], key: str
 277 │ ) -> str | AbstractSet[str]:
 278 │     try:
 279 │         return environment[key]
 280 │     except KeyError:
 281 │         raise UndefinedEnvironmentName(key) from None

 283 │ 
 284 │ def _evaluate_markers(
 285 │     markers: MarkerList, environment: dict[str, str | AbstractSet[str]]
 286 │ ) -> bool:
 287 │     groups: list[list[bool]] = [[]]
 288 │ 
 289 │     for marker in markers:
 290 │         if isinstance(marker, list):
 291 │             groups[-1].append(_evaluate_markers(marker, environment))
 292 │         elif isinstance(marker, tuple):
 293 │             lhs, op, rhs = marker
 294 │ 
 295 │             if isinstance(lhs, Variable):
 296 │                 environment_key = lhs.value
 297 │                 lhs_value = _lookup_environment(environment, environment_key)
 298 │                 rhs_value = rhs.value
 299 │             else:
 300 │                 lhs_value = lhs.value
 301 │                 environment_key = rhs.value
 302 │                 rhs_value = _lookup_environment(environment, environment_key)
 303 │ 
 304 │             if not isinstance(lhs_value, str):
 305 │                 raise UndefinedComparison(
 306 │                     f"Set-valued marker {environment_key!r} can only be used "
 307 │                     f'with the membership form (e.g. "<name>" in '
 308 │                     f"{environment_key}); it cannot appear on the left-hand "
 309 │                     f"side of {op.serialize()!r}."
 310 │                 )
 311 │             lhs_value, rhs_value = _normalize(lhs_value, rhs_value, key=environment_key)
 312 │             groups[-1].append(_eval_op(lhs_value, op, rhs_value, key=environment_key))
 313 │         elif marker == "or":
 314 │             groups.append([])
 315 │         elif marker == "and":
 316 │             pass
 317 │         else:  # pragma: nocover
 318 │             raise TypeError(f"Unexpected marker {marker!r}")
 319 │ 
 320 │     return any(all(item) for item in groups)

 323 │ def _format_full_version(info: sys._version_info) -> str:
 324 │     version = f"{info.major}.{info.minor}.{info.micro}"
 325 │     kind = info.releaselevel
 326 │     if kind != "final":
 327 │         version += kind[0] + str(info.serial)
 328 │     return version

 331 │ @functools.cache
 332 │ def _cached_default_environment() -> Environment:
 333 │     """Build the default marker environment for the current Python process.
 334 │ 
 335 │     The values are derived from process-constant data (the running interpreter
 336 │     and the host platform), so this is cached and built only once. The result is
 337 │     shared between callers and must never be mutated; :func:`default_environment`
 338 │     returns a fresh copy.
 339 │     """
 340 │     iver = _format_full_version(sys.implementation.version)
 341 │     implementation_name = sys.implementation.name
 342 │     return {
 343 │         "implementation_name": implementation_name,
 344 │         "implementation_version": iver,
 345 │         "os_name": os.name,
 346 │         "platform_machine": platform.machine(),
 347 │         "platform_release": platform.release(),
 348 │         "platform_system": platform.system(),
 349 │         "platform_version": platform.version(),
 350 │         "python_full_version": platform.python_version(),
 351 │         "platform_python_implementation": platform.python_implementation(),
 352 │         "python_version": ".".join(platform.python_version_tuple()[:2]),

 357 │ def default_environment() -> Environment:
 358 │     """Return the default marker environment for the current Python process.
 359 │ 
 360 │     This is the base environment used by :meth:`Marker.evaluate`. A fresh copy
 361 │     is returned on every call so callers may freely mutate the result; a shallow
 362 │     copy suffices because all values are immutable strings.
 363 │ 
 364 │     .. versionchanged:: 26.3
 365 │         The environment is computed once per process and cached, since it is
 366 │         derived from process-constant data. Patching ``platform``/``sys``/``os``
 367 │         after the first call has no effect; pass an explicit ``environment`` to
 368 │         :meth:`Marker.evaluate` to evaluate against different values.
 369 │     """
 370 │     return cast("Environment", dict(_cached_default_environment()))

 373 │ class Marker:
 374 │     """Represents a parsed dependency marker expression.
 375 │ 
 376 │     Marker expressions are parsed according to the
 377 │     :ref:`specification of dependency specifiers <pypug:dependency-specifiers>`.
 378 │ 
 379 │     :param marker: The string representation of a marker expression.
 380 │     :raises InvalidMarker: If ``marker`` cannot be parsed.
 381 │ 
 382 │     Instances are safe to serialize with :mod:`pickle`. They use a stable
 383 │     format so the same pickle can be loaded in future packaging releases.
 384 │ 
 385 │     .. versionchanged:: 26.2
 386 │ 
 387 │         Added a stable pickle format. Pickles created with packaging 26.2+ can
 388 │         be unpickled with future releases.  Backward compatibility with pickles
 389 │         from packaging < 26.2 is supported but may be removed in a future
 390 │         release.
 391 │     """
 392 │ 
 393 │     __slots__ = ("_markers",)
 394 │ 
 395 │     def __init__(self, marker: str) -> None:
 396 │         # Note: We create a Marker object without calling this constructor in
 397 │         #       packaging.requirements.Requirement. If any additional logic is
 398 │         #       added here, make sure to mirror/adapt Requirement.
 399 │ 
 400 │         # If this fails and throws an error, the repr still expects _markers to
 401 │         # be defined.
 402 │         self._markers: MarkerList = []
 403 │ 
 404 │         try:
 405 │             self._markers = _normalize_extra_values(_parse_marker(marker))
 406 │             # The attribute `_markers` can be described in terms of a recursive type:
 407 │             # MarkerList = List[Union[Tuple[Node, ...], str, MarkerList]]
 408 │             #
 409 │             # For example, the following expression:
 410 │             # python_version > "3.6" or (python_version == "3.6" and os_name == "unix")
 411 │             #
 412 │             # is parsed into:
 413 │             # [
 414 │             #     (<Variable('python_version')>, <Op('>')>, <Value('3.6')>),
 415 │             #     'and',
 416 │             #     [
 417 │             #         (<Variable('python_version')>, <Op('==')>, <Value('3.6')>),
 418 │             #         'or',
 419 │             #         (<Variable('os_name')>, <Op('==')>, <Value('unix')>)
 420 │             #     ]
 421 │             # ]
 422 │         except ParserSyntaxError as e:
 423 │             raise InvalidMarker(str(e)) from e
 424 │ 
 425 │     @classmethod
 426 │     def _from_markers(cls, markers: MarkerList) -> Marker:
 427 │         """Create a Marker instance from a pre-parsed marker tree.
 428 │ 
 429 │         This avoids re-parsing serialised marker strings when combining markers.
 430 │         """
 431 │         new = cls.__new__(cls)
 432 │         new._markers = markers
 433 │         return new
 434 │ 
 435 │     def __str__(self) -> str:
 436 │         return _format_marker(self._markers)
 437 │ 
 438 │     def __repr__(self) -> str:
 439 │         return f"<{self.__class__.__name__}({str(self)!r})>"
 440 │ 
 441 │     def __hash__(self) -> int:
 442 │         return hash(str(self))
 443 │ 
 444 │     def __eq__(self, other: object) -> bool:
 445 │         if not isinstance(other, Marker):
 446 │             return NotImplemented
 447 │ 
 448 │         return str(self) == str(other)
 449 │ 
 450 │     def __getstate__(self) -> str:
 451 │         # Return the marker expression string for compactness and stability.
 452 │         # Internal Node objects are excluded; the string is re-parsed on load.
 453 │         return str(self)
 454 │ 
 455 │     def __setstate__(self, state: object) -> None:
 456 │         if isinstance(state, str):
 457 │             # New format (26.2+): just the marker expression string.
 458 │             try:
 459 │                 self._markers = _normalize_extra_values(_parse_marker(state))
 460 │             except ParserSyntaxError as exc:
 461 │                 raise TypeError(f"Cannot restore Marker from {state!r}") from exc
 462 │             return
 463 │         if isinstance(state, dict) and "_markers" in state:
 464 │             # Old format (packaging <= 26.1, no __slots__): plain __dict__.
 465 │             markers = state["_markers"]

 467 │                 self._markers = markers
 468 │                 return
 469 │         if isinstance(state, tuple) and len(state) == 2:
 470 │             # Old format (packaging <= 26.1, __slots__): (None, {slot: value}).
 471 │             _, slot_dict = state
 472 │             if isinstance(slot_dict, dict) and "_markers" in slot_dict:
 473 │                 markers = slot_dict["_markers"]
 474 │                 if isinstance(markers, list):
 475 │                     self._markers = markers
 476 │                     return
 477 │         raise TypeError(f"Cannot restore Marker from {state!r}")
 478 │ 
 479 │     def __and__(self, other: Marker) -> Marker:
 480 │         """Combine this marker with another using ``and``.
 481 │ 
 482 │         .. versionadded:: 26.1
 483 │         """
 484 │         if not isinstance(other, Marker):
 485 │             return NotImplemented
 486 │         return self._from_markers([self._markers, "and", other._markers])
 487 │ 
 488 │     def __or__(self, other: Marker) -> Marker:
 489 │         """Combine this marker with another using ``or``.
 490 │ 
 491 │         .. versionadded:: 26.1
 492 │         """
 493 │         if not isinstance(other, Marker):
 494 │             return NotImplemented
 495 │         return self._from_markers([self._markers, "or", other._markers])

 497 │     def evaluate(
 498 │         self,
 499 │         environment: Mapping[str, str | AbstractSet[str]] | None = None,
 500 │         context: EvaluateContext = "metadata",
 501 │     ) -> bool:
 502 │         """Evaluate a marker.
 503 │ 
 504 │         Return the boolean from evaluating this marker against the environment.
 505 │         The environment is determined from the current Python process unless
 506 │         passed in explicitly.
 507 │ 
 508 │         :param environment: Mapping containing keys and values to override the
 509 │            detected environment.
 510 │         :param EvaluateContext context: The context in which the marker is
 511 │             evaluated, which influences what marker names are considered valid.
 512 │             Accepted values are ``"metadata"`` (for core metadata; default),
 513 │             ``"lock_file"``, and ``"requirement"`` (i.e. all other situations).
 514 │         :raises UndefinedComparison: If the marker uses a comparison on values
 515 │             that are not valid versions per the :ref:`specification of version
 516 │             specifiers <pypug:version-specifiers>`.
 517 │         :raises UndefinedEnvironmentName: If the marker references a value that
 518 │             is missing from the evaluation environment.
 519 │         :returns: ``True`` if the marker matches, otherwise ``False``.
 520 │ 
 521 │         """
 522 │         current_environment = cast(
 523 │             "dict[str, str | AbstractSet[str]]", default_environment()
 524 │         )
 525 │         if context == "lock_file":
 526 │             current_environment |= {
 527 │                 "extras": frozenset(),
 528 │                 "dependency_groups": frozenset(),
 529 │             }
 530 │         elif context == "metadata":
 531 │             current_environment["extra"] = ""
 532 │ 
 533 │         if environment is not None:
 534 │             current_environment |= environment
 535 │             if "extra" in current_environment:
 536 │                 # The API used to allow setting extra to None. We need to handle
 537 │                 # this case for backwards compatibility. Also skip running
 538 │                 # normalize name if extra is empty.
 539 │                 extra = cast("str | None", current_environment["extra"])
 540 │                 current_environment["extra"] = canonicalize_name(extra) if extra else ""
 541 │ 
 542 │         return _evaluate_markers(
 543 │             self._markers, _repair_python_full_version(current_environment)
 544 │         )
 545 │ 
 546 │ 
 547 │ def _pep440_python_full_version(python_full_version: str) -> str:
 548 │     """
 549 │     Work around platform.python_version() returning something that is not PEP 440
 550 │     compliant for non-tagged Python builds.
 551 │     """
 552 │     if python_full_version.endswith("+"):
 553 │         return f"{python_full_version}local"
 554 │     return python_full_version

 557 │ def _repair_python_full_version(
 558 │     env: dict[str, str | AbstractSet[str]],
 559 │ ) -> dict[str, str | AbstractSet[str]]:
 560 │     """
 561 │     Work around platform.python_version() returning something that is not PEP 440
 562 │     compliant for non-tagged Python builds.
 563 │     """
 564 │     python_full_version = cast("str", env["python_full_version"])
 565 │     env["python_full_version"] = _pep440_python_full_version(python_full_version)

 110 │ def _parse_requirement(tokenizer: Tokenizer) -> ParsedRequirement:
 111 │     """
 112 │     requirement = WS? IDENTIFIER WS? extras WS? requirement_details
 113 │     """
 114 │     tokenizer.consume("WS")
 115 │ 
 116 │     name_token = tokenizer.expect(
 117 │         "IDENTIFIER", expected="package name at the start of dependency specifier"
 118 │     )
 119 │     name = name_token.text
 120 │     tokenizer.consume("WS")
 121 │ 
 122 │     extras = _parse_extras(tokenizer)
 123 │     tokenizer.consume("WS")
 124 │ 
 125 │     url, specifier, marker = _parse_requirement_details(tokenizer)
 126 │     tokenizer.expect("END", expected="end of dependency specifier")
 127 │ 
 128 │     return ParsedRequirement(name, url, extras, specifier, marker)

 131 │ def _parse_requirement_details(
 132 │     tokenizer: Tokenizer,
 133 │ ) -> tuple[str, str, MarkerList | None]:
 134 │     """
 135 │     requirement_details = AT URL (WS requirement_marker?)?
 136 │                         | specifier WS? (requirement_marker)?
 137 │     """
 138 │ 
 139 │     specifier = ""
 140 │     url = ""
 141 │     marker = None
 142 │ 
 143 │     if tokenizer.check("AT"):
 144 │         tokenizer.read()
 145 │         tokenizer.consume("WS")
 146 │ 
 147 │         url_start = tokenizer.position
 148 │         url = tokenizer.expect("URL", expected="URL after @").text
 149 │         if tokenizer.check("END", peek=True):
 150 │             return (url, specifier, marker)
 151 │ 
 152 │         tokenizer.expect("WS", expected="whitespace after URL")
 153 │ 
 154 │         # The input might end after whitespace.
 155 │         if tokenizer.check("END", peek=True):
 156 │             return (url, specifier, marker)
 157 │ 
 158 │         marker = _parse_requirement_marker(
 159 │             tokenizer,
 160 │             span_start=url_start,
 161 │             expected="semicolon (after URL and whitespace)",
 162 │         )
 163 │     else:
 164 │         specifier_start = tokenizer.position
 165 │         specifier = _parse_specifier(tokenizer)
 166 │         tokenizer.consume("WS")
 167 │ 
 168 │         if tokenizer.check("END", peek=True):
 169 │             return (url, specifier, marker)
 170 │ 
 171 │         marker = _parse_requirement_marker(
 172 │             tokenizer,
 173 │             span_start=specifier_start,
 174 │             expected=(
 175 │                 "comma (within version specifier), semicolon (after version specifier)"
 176 │                 if specifier
 177 │                 else "semicolon (after name with no version specifier)"
 178 │             ),
 179 │         )
 180 │ 
 181 │     return (url, specifier, marker)

 184 │ def _parse_requirement_marker(

 186 │ ) -> MarkerList:

 194 │             span_start=span_start,

 196 │         )
 197 │     tokenizer.read()
 198 │ 
 199 │     marker = _parse_marker(tokenizer)
 200 │     tokenizer.consume("WS")
